newsitem.title: USA: IMF ready to aid Albania once government in place.
newsitem.headline: IMF ready to aid Albania once government in place.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is ready to move quickly to aid Albania once its new government is in place, an IMF official said on Thursday.

"We're waiting for the government to be formed after which the fund would be prepared to move quickly to discuss a (economic reform) program supported by (IMF) resources," said the official, who declined to be named.
The IMF would likely send a mission to work with the country's leaders to negotiate the terms of the program.
Incomplete returns from Sunday's first round of elections have given the Socialists under economist Fatos Nano a big lead.

President Sali Berisha has admitted the defeat of his Democratic Party and said he will step down when a leftist government comes to power. Run-off elections will be held on Sunday in districts where no candidate got the required 50 percent of the vote.
The IMF has disbursed some $60 million in credits to Albania since 1992, but the program was suspended in 1995. The World Bank has dished out some $300 million in loans.
